chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who kicked a woman in her private area, and she claimed that she no longer menstruates, while her menstruation had been regular. He said: 'She is observed for one year. If her menstruation returns, then nothing is required. But if it does not return, the man must pay one-third of her blood money for the damage to her menstruation and the harm caused to her womb.'
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a man who kicks a woman in her private part causing her to stop menstruating?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing a one-year diagnostic period to distinguish between temporary trauma and permanent infertility (fasad al-tamth). If menstruation does not resume, the perpetrator is liable for one-third of the full blood money (diya), specifically compensating for the loss of the menstrual function and uterine integrity, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on precise bodily damages.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Abu Abdullah (as) was asked about a man who kicked a woman in her private area, and she claimed that her menstruation had stopped while it was previously regular.
Imam (as) said: "She should be observed for one year. If her menstruation returns, then nothing is required. But if it does not return, the man must pay one-third of her blood money (diyyah) for the damage to her menstruation and the harm caused to her womb."
